faqs.question: What is a good garba partner quote in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: A short two-line duha works best, for example ગરબે ફરતી આંખડી, શોધે તારું નામ; તાળી ચૂકું તાલમાં, દિલ ના બોલે આમ (Garbe pharti ankhdi, shodhe taru naam; taali chuku taalma, dil na bole aam). It means: my eyes, circling in the garba, look for your name; I miss the clap, yet my heart won't say it aloud.

faqs.question: How do I say "my garba partner" in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: Say મારો ગરબા પાર્ટનર (maro garba partner) for a male partner and મારી ગરબા પાર્ટનર (mari garba partner) for a female one. Avoid ભાગીદાર (bhagidar), which means a business partner.

faqs.question: Is garba partner shayari in Gujarati the same as a duha?
faqs.answer: Not strictly. Shayari is the Urdu tradition of the sher and ghazal, while the duha is the two-line verse of Gujarati folk poetry. People search for Gujarati shayari when they want any short romantic verse, and a duha does that job in a native form.

faqs.question: What is a duha in Gujarati poetry?
faqs.answer: A duha (દુહો) is a self-contained two-line verse from Gujarati folk literature, the Gujarati form of the doha. The Bhagavadgomandal dictionary says one duha usually needs no other to be understood.

faqs.question: How many mātrā does a duha have?
faqs.answer: The classical count is 13 mātrā in the first and third parts and 11 in the second and fourth, so 24 per line, with both lines rhyming. A long vowel or anusvara counts 2, a short vowel 1.

faqs.question: Are these Gujarati garba quotes copied from garba songs?
faqs.answer: No. All 14 quotes on this page are original. Garba song lyrics and collected folk verses belong to their writers and singers, so we name the tradition but quote none of them.

faqs.question: Who was Jhaverchand Meghani?
faqs.answer: Jhaverchand Meghani (1897–1947) was a Gujarati writer who travelled across Saurashtra collecting folk stories, songs and ballads, published as Saurashtrani Rasdhar between 1923 and 1927. Gandhi called him the national poet, Rashtriya Shayar.

faqs.question: Can I send a Gujarati quote to someone who doesn't read Gujarati script?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you add the romanised line underneath, as every quote here does. Send it to yourself first, because conjuncts such as પ્ર are where a missing Gujarati font shows.

faqs.question: When should I send a garba partner quote in Navratri 2026?
faqs.answer: Sharad Navratri 2026 runs from 11 to 19 October, with garba again on Sharad Purnima, 25 October. Send the shy lines in the first three nights; the 'tenth day' duha is for Dussehra, 20 October in Delhi and 21 October in Bengal and Mysuru.

faqs.question: Can I put these quotes in the Be My Dandiya Partner invitation?
faqs.answer: Yes. It holds nine short lines, one per night, so the eight duhas plus one line of your own fill it. Its buttons and menus are in English, so the Gujarati lines sit inside an English interface.

faqs.question: Should I use a garba partner quote to invite my whole society?
faqs.answer: No. These quotes and the Be My Dandiya Partner page are one-to-one, for a love, a crush or a best friend. For a society, office or family group, a group message or printed notice fits better.

# Garba Partner Quotes in Gujarati: 8 Duhas and 6 Lines to Send

Here are 14 original garba partner quotes in Gujarati: eight two-line દુહા (duha, the Gujarati doha couplet) and six shorter lines, sorted by mood: shy, playful, devotional-romantic and long-distance. Each comes in Gujarati script, romanised and in English.

On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so every quote fits a phone screen without scrolling. And timing matters: in our nearest festival measurement, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89 pages), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself. That is a rakhi figure, not Navratri data, but it suggests most people write on the night.

Below: what a duha is, the quotes, where each format works, and when it is the wrong choice.

## What is a duha, and why does it suit a garba partner quote?

A duha (દુહો, duho) is a self-contained two-line verse from Gujarati folk poetry. The [Bhagavadgomandal entry for દુહો](http://www.bhagavadgomandal.com/index.php?action=dictionary&sitem=%E0%AA%A6%E0%AB%81%E0%AA%B9%E0%AB%8B&type=3&page=0) calls it a two-line દોહરો that usually needs no second duha to be understood, holding the place in folk literature that the anushtup shloka holds in Sanskrit maxims.

The metre is strict. The [Hindi Wiktionary entry for दोहा](https://hi.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%BE) gives 13 mātrā (beats) in the first and third parts, 11 in the second and fourth, and a rhyme closing both lines.

Jhaverchand Meghani called the duha "a sensitive precision scale" in [Elegiac Chhand and Duha in Charani Lore](https://web.archive.org/web/20240225010304/https://asianethnology.org/article/644/download) (Asian Folklore Studies 59, 2000), and rejected the idea that any two rhyming lines make one. He wrote that it carries "the ecstasy of romance" and "the anguish of the parted", which is the range a garba partner quote needs.

## 8 original Gujarati duhas for your garba partner, by mood

Each duha keeps the 13 + 11 count: a long vowel or anusvara is 2 mātrā, a short vowel 1, and a short vowel before a conjunct inside a word 2. So ગ-ર-બે is 1 + 1 + 2.

### 1. Shy: for the person you have not asked yet

**ગરબે ફરતી આંખડી, શોધે તારું નામ;**
**તાળી ચૂકું તાલમાં, દિલ ના બોલે આમ.**

*Garbe pharti ankhdi, shodhe taru naam; / Taali chuku taalma, dil na bole aam.*

My eyes, circling in the garba, look for your name; I miss the clap in the beat, yet my heart won't say it aloud.

**ચોકે ઊભો એકલો, જોઉં તારો તાલ;**
**પૂછું કે ના પૂછવું, વીતી આઠમ કાલ.**

*Choke ubho eklo, jou taro taal; / Puchhu ke na puchhvu, viti Aatham kaal.*

Standing alone at the edge of the chowk, I watch your rhythm; to ask or not to ask, and Ashtami went by yesterday.

### 2. Playful: for the partner who steps on your foot

**દાંડી મારી તૂટશે, તારી સાથે રાસ;**
**તોય ન મૂકું હાથ હું, આખી રાત ઉજાસ.**

*Dandi mari tutshe, tari sathe raas; / Toy na muku haath hu, aakhi raat ujaas.*

Playing raas with you, my stick will break; still I won't let go of your hand, and the whole night stays lit.

**ભૂલી તાળી બે વખત, મારા પગ પર પાય;**
**હસી પડી, ભૂલી ગઈ, ગરબાનો એ ન્યાય.**

*Bhuli taali be vakhat, mara pag par paay; / Hasi padi, bhuli gai, garbano e nyaay.*

You missed the clap twice and your foot landed on mine; I laughed and let it go, that is garba's own justice.

### 3. Devotional-romantic: for the night of the aarti

**માના ગરબે દીવડો, તારે મુખે પ્રકાશ;**
**અંબે પાસે માગણું, બસ તારો સહવાસ.**

*Maa na garbe divdo, taare mukhe prakash; / Ambe paase maagnu, bas taro sahvaas.*

A small lamp in the Mother's garbo, its light on your face; all I ask of Amba is your company.

**નવ દીવા, નવ રાતડી, માડી, તને પ્રણામ;**
**દસમે દિવસે માગજે હાથ, હૃદય ને નામ.**

*Nav diva, nav raatdi, Maadi, tane pranaam; / Dasme divse maagje haath, hriday ne naam.*

Nine lamps, nine nights, Mother, I bow to you; on the tenth day, ask me for my hand, my heart and my name.

### 4. Long-distance: for a partner in another city or country

**તું પરદેશે, હું અહીં, વચ્ચે દરિયા સાત;**
**ફોને ગરબો ઘૂમજે મારી સાથે રાત.**

*Tu pardeshe, hu ahin, vachche dariya saat; / Phone garbo ghumje mari sathe raat.*

You abroad, me here, seven seas between us; dance the garba on the phone with me tonight.

**ખાલી જગ્યા ચોકમાં તારી રાખી આજ;**
**પાછો આવી ખેલજે, ગરબો તારે કાજ.**

*Khaali jagya chokma tari raakhi aaj; / Pachho aavi khelje, garbo taare kaaj.*

Tonight I kept your place empty in the chowk; come back and play, this garba is for you.

## 6 short "my garba partner" quotes in Gujarati

Not every partner wants verse. These lines use મારો (maro) for a male partner and મારી (mari) for a female one. Skip ભાગીદાર (bhagidar): it means a business partner, and turns a crush into a shareholder.

1. **આખા ચોકમાં સો ખેલૈયા છે, પણ મારી તાળી ફક્ત તારા તાલ પર ચૂકે છે.** *Aakha chokma so khelaiya chhe, pan mari taali fakt tara taal par chuke chhe.* A hundred players in the chowk, and my clap misses the beat only on yours. (Shy)
2. **તું મારી ગરબા પાર્ટનર બનીશ? ના હોય તો પણ એક ફેરો તો સાથે ફરીએ.** *Tu mari garba partner banish? Na hoy to pan ek phero to sathe pharie.* Will you be my garba partner? Even if it's a no, let's do one round together. (Shy)
3. **મારો ગરબા પાર્ટનર એ છે જે મારા પગ પર પગ મૂકે, ને પછી દોષ મને જ આપે.** *Maro garba partner e chhe je mara pag par pag muke, ne pachhi dosh mane j aape.* My garba partner steps on my foot and then blames me. (Playful)
4. **નવ રાત, નવ ચણિયાચોળી, ને એક જ સવાલ: "આજે કયો રંગ?"** *Nav raat, nav chaniyacholi, ne ek j savaal: "Aaje kayo rang?"* Nine nights, nine chaniya-cholis, one question: "Which colour tonight?" (Playful)
5. **માતાજીનો ગરબો વચ્ચે, ને આપણે બંને એની ફરતે; આથી સાચું વચન બીજું શું?** *Mataji no garbo vachche, ne aapne banne eni pharte; aathi saachu vachan biju shu?* The Mother's garbo in the middle, the two of us circling it; what promise could be truer? (Devotional-romantic)
6. **અહીં રાતના દસ, ત્યાં બપોર; પણ ઢોલ તો બંનેના હૈયામાં એક જ તાલે.** *Ahin raatna das, tyaan bapor; pan dhol to bannena haiyama ek j taale.* Ten at night here, afternoon there; but the dhol beats in both our hearts to one rhythm. (Long-distance)

Line 6 fits New York, where 10 pm in India is 12:30 pm in October.

## Where Gujarati garba poetry comes from: Meghani and lok-sahitya

Gujarati folk poetry, લોકસાહિત્ય (lok-sahitya), was sung long before it was printed. Krupa Shah's paper on [Jhaverchand Meghani and Saurashtrani Rasdhar](http://www.ntm.org.in/download/ttvol/volume11-1/Art_1.pdf) (Translation Today 11, 2017) describes how Meghani (1897–1947) travelled across Saurashtra for years, documenting folk stories, songs and ballads from people of many castes, occupations and genders. *Saurashtrani Rasdhar* appeared between 1923 and 1927, and Gandhi called him રાષ્ટ્રીય શાયર, the national poet.

Meghani's own essay places the duha inside that oral world: "the entire class of duhas" belongs to folk song, and the duhas of the Son and Halaman romance are at least 1,500 years old.

We have not quoted any collected verse here. Those lines belong to their singers, and a garba partner quote lands better when it is yours.

## Which format to send, and where

The last column is SubhSandesh's own platform-wide measurement, not Navratri data.

| Format | Length | Best place | What our data says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duha (2 lines) | 24 mātrā a line, 6–8 words | WhatsApp status, Story text | 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone |
| One-line quote | 10–20 words | Instagram Story, chat | 48.4% of views are on a phone or tablet |
| Quote inside a private invitation | 9 lines, one per night | One person, private link | 38.5% of creators password-protect their page |
| Quote written on the night | Any | Same-day send | 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the day (n = 89) |

A duha is the right length for a status; a private page suits the line you would not post publicly.

## Sending your quote as a one-to-one garba invitation

If your quote is really a question, put it in the [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner). It holds nine short lines, one for each night of Navratri, so the eight duhas above plus one of your own fill it exactly.

The recipient lights nine diyas round a garbo, each revealing one line, and picks the colour they will twirl in. Tap No, and it twirls away with a new excuse, turning into a second Yes after five tries.

Two honest notes. The page's buttons and menus are in English, so your Gujarati lines sit inside an English interface. And it is a one-to-one invitation for a love, a crush or a best friend as garba buddy, so it is the wrong tool for a society, office or family group.

For a partner in another city, an invitation to a dance they cannot attend can sting. The [miss-you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) suits the long-distance duhas better: it says what you feel without asking them to turn up.

## When to send: the nights in 2026 and 2027

Sharad Navratri 2026 runs from Sunday 11 October to Monday 19 October, when Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami share a day in New Delhi, per [Drik Panchang's 2026 Navratri calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2026). Gujarat plays garba again on Sharad Purnima, Sunday 25 October 2026. In 2027, Navratri runs from 30 September to 8 October.

Send the shy duhas in the first three nights. The "tenth day" duha is written for Dussehra: 20 October 2026 in Delhi, 21 October in Bengal and Mysuru.

## When a Gujarati duha, or our page, is the wrong choice

A duha fails when your partner cannot read Gujarati script and you have dropped the romanised line. Conjuncts such as પ્ર in પ્રણામ are where a missing Gujarati font shows first, so send the line to yourself before posting. Verse about the Mother's lamp is too heavy for someone you barely know; send a playful one-liner.

Our invitation loses in three cases: group invites, a partner who wants a Gujarati interface, and anyone after a garba pass. It sells no passes and does not find or rent you a partner. In the same sheri garba, a line said aloud beats any link.
